If you weren't home, would anyone else know how your house works?

Important details often live in one person's head. Where the water shutoff is, which filter fits the HVAC system, or who to call when something breaks. That becomes a problem when someone else needs to handle things.

I created The Home Systems Record to help organize those details: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

Every house has its own unwritten instruction manual.

Someone knows where the main water shutoff is, which HVAC filter to buy, and who serviced the furnace last winter. But that information isn't always shared with everyone who lives there.

Try asking another person in your household three questions: Where's the water shutoff? What's the HVAC filter size? Who's our usual repair contact? Write down anything that's unclear.

A home is easier to manage when important information isn't dependent on one person's memory.

Equipment locations, service contacts, appliance details, and document locations are all worth recording somewhere accessible. It gives other household members a starting point when they need to help.

The Home Systems Record includes 12 printable worksheets for organizing that information: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

A useful household reference doesn't need to become a complicated organization project.

A few clearly labeled pages can help family members find essential system locations, equipment details, and service contacts. The most important part is making sure people know where the reference lives.

Try creating a simple three-section binder: Important Locations, Equipment Details, and Service Contacts. Show everyone in the household where to find it.

A well-documented home is easier to care for together.

When household members can find equipment information, important locations, and repair contacts, they have a better starting point for handling everyday maintenance. Shared records won't solve every problem, but they can reduce unnecessary guesswork.

The Home Systems Record offers a printable way to organize those details: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

It's easy for one person to become the unofficial keeper of all the household information.

They know the appliance models, the repair contacts, and where the important documents are stored. Everything works fine until they're unavailable and someone else needs an answer. A shared home reference can make those moments easier.

What's one important detail about your home that only one person in your household seems to know?
